sumInsured: As per Policy Schedule (not specified in provided extract)

great.name: Room Rent
great.quote: The eligible Room Rent or Room Category applicable for the Insured Person under the Policy is 'No limit', which means that there is no separate restriction on Room Charges incurred towards stay during Hospitalization
great.explanation: Room rent is on a 'No limit' basis during hospitalization. This lets you choose any room category without room-rent-linked deductions.

great.name: ICU Charges
great.quote: Intensive Care Unit Charges (ICU Charges): The eligible ICU Charges applicable for the Insured Person under the Policy is 'No limit'
great.explanation: ICU charges are covered with 'No limit' under the policy. This reduces the risk of large out-of-pocket costs during critical care.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: automatically make the re-instatement of up to the base Sum Insured unlimited times in a policy year... Recharge amount can be utilized for same illness as well as different Illnesses.
great.explanation: Base Sum Insured is reinstated unlimited times in a policy year. The recharged amount can be used for the same illness as well as different illnesses, which is stronger than typical restores.

great.name: NCB
great.quote: enhance the Sum Insured by 50% flat, on a cumulative basis... (vi) In the event of a Claim there is no impact on the accrual of Cumulative Bonus.
great.explanation: Sum Insured increases by a flat 50% cumulatively as Cumulative Bonus. Even if you make a claim, the accrual of Cumulative Bonus is not impacted, so your bonus does not reset.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: For any single Claim during a Policy Year, the maximum Claim amount payable shall be sum total of Sum Insured, Cumulative Bonus , Cumulative Bonus Super (if applicable), Plus Benefit (if applicable), Unlimited Care (if applicable).
great.explanation: For a single claim, the maximum payable can be the total of Sum Insured plus add-ons like Cumulative Bonus and other applicable benefits. This can increase the claim-paying capacity beyond the base Sum Insured when those benefits exist.

great.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
great.quote: The Company will indemnify the Insured Person... for the Medical Expenses incurred towards Domiciliary Hospitalization
great.explanation: Medical expenses for domiciliary hospitalization are covered as per policy terms. This helps when treatment is taken at home instead of in a hospital.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered for the first 36 months of continuous coverage. Claims for declared/known conditions will be payable only after this waiting period ends.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Listed specific illnesses are excluded for 24 months of continuous coverage. You should expect no payout for those conditions until the 2-year wait is completed.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered for the first 30 days from policy start, except accidents. This is the standard initial waiting period in retail health insurance.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: For a period of 60 days immediately prior to the Insured Person's date of admission to the Hospital
good.explanation: Pre-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for up to 60 days before admission. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to hospitalization.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: For a period of 180 days immediately after the Insured Person's date of discharge from the hospital
good.explanation: Post-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for up to 180 days after discharge. This supports follow-up treatment and medicines for a longer recovery period.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: The Company will indemnify the Insured Person up to the amount as specified in Policy Schedule , for the Reasonable and Customary Charges necessarily incurred on availing Air Ambulance services
good.explanation: Air ambulance expenses are covered up to the amount specified in the Policy Schedule. This can be valuable for emergency transfers but is limited to the scheduled cap.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure – I to Policy Terms & Conditions).
bad.reference: Clause 4.2(1), page 37 and Annexure I (List I – Optional Items) pages 58-59
bad.explanation: Items listed as non-medical/consumables in Annexure I are excluded from claims. This can increase out-of-pocket costs for common hospital items unless covered via an add-on.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: For diseases or conditions or procedure that have a specified sub-limit then all related expenses shall be covered up to the sub-limit specified for that disease or condition or procedure.
bad.explanation: If a disease/procedure has a specified sub-limit, all related expenses are payable only up to that sub-limit. This can significantly reduce payouts even when your Sum Insured is higher.

bad.name: Co-pay (Optional)
bad.quote: The Co-payment proportion ( If opted ) shall be borne by the Insured Person on each Claim...
bad.reference: General Conditions, Clause 4, page 14 and Optional Benefit 3.2.7, page 24-25
bad.explanation: A co-payment applies on each claim if this option is opted. This means you will bear a percentage of every admissible claim, which increases your out-of-pocket cost.
